items.text: Recapitulation
Two non-tautological facts on sheaves over $X$:
\operatorname{Top}(X)\simeq\operatorname{Et}(X)
\operatorname{Hom}(P,iF)=\operatorname{Hom}(aP,F)\qquad(a\dashv i,\ \ P\mapsto \tilde P)
and $a$ is left exact (it commutes with direct limits, being a left adjoint).
A neat proof of both together (a remark of Schanuel), not in the literature as far as he knows. First, stalks.
Stalks
$P$ a presheaf, $x\in X$: the open neighbourhoods $U$ of $x$ form a filtering set.
P_x=\varinjlim_{U\ni x}P(U)\qquad\text{germs } f_x\ \text{of sections } f\in P(U)
P\mapsto P_x=\varinjlim_{U\ni x}\bigl(P\mapsto P(U)\bigr)
Each $P\mapsto P(U)$ commutes with all limits; a direct limit of functors commutes with direct limits.
A filtering direct limit of left exact functors is left exact.
P\mapsto P_x\ \text{ commutes with all direct limits and finite inverse limits}
Same for sheaves: inverse limits of sheaves are those of presheaves, so $\mathrm{St}_x$ is left exact.
P_x\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }(\tilde P)_x\quad\forall x
Admitted for now (comes out of the proof below). Consequence for sheaves:
\varinjlim^{\text{sheaves}}F_i=\widetilde{\varinjlim^{\text{pre}}F_i},\qquad \bigl(\varinjlim F_i\bigr)_x=\varinjlim (F_i)_x
So $\mathrm{St}_x\colon\operatorname{Top}(X)\to\mathbf{Sets}$ commutes with all direct limits and finite inverse limits ($F_x=\mathrm{St}_x(F)$).
Stalks are jointly conservative
u\colon F\to G\ \text{iso}\iff \forall x\in X:\ u_x\colon F_x\xrightarrow{\sim}G_x
False for presheaves. Injective: $f\in F(V)$ with $u(f)$ given; then all germs $f_x$ are known.
Germ known = section known near $x$; $F$ a sheaf: $f$ is known.
Surjective: $g\in G(V)$.
\forall x\in V\ \exists\, V_x\ni x,\ f_x\in F(V_x):\quad u(f_x)=g|_{V_x}
On $V_x\cap V_y$: $u(f_x)=u(f_y)$, $u$ injective, so $f_x=f_y$ there: they glue.
Used: $F$ a sheaf, $G$ only separated.
The two functors $\Phi$, $\Psi$
Fibre spaces over $X$ contain the open sets as spaces $U\hookrightarrow X$.
\Phi\colon \operatorname{Fib}(X)\to\hat{\mathcal O},\qquad \Phi(E)(U)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(U,E)
$\Phi$ restricts to $\operatorname{Et}(X)\to\operatorname{Top}(X)$.
It has a left adjoint $\Psi$:
\operatorname{Hom}_X(\Psi P,E)=\operatorname{Hom}(P,\Phi E)
Construction of $\Psi(P)$
\Psi(P)=\coprod_{x\in X}P_x\ \longrightarrow\ X
Topology: generated by the sets $D_f$, for $f\in P(U)$.
D_f=\{f_x: x\in U\}\subset\Psi(P)
D_f\cap D_g=D_h,\quad h=f|_W=g|_W,\ \ W=\{\text{points of } U\cap V \text{ where } f_x=g_x\}
Open sets = unions of $D_f$.
D_f\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }U\ \ \text{homeomorphism, for } f\in P(U)
So $\Psi(P)$ is glued from open pieces over $X$: étale. Everything else is straightforward checking.
A map out of $\Psi(P)$ = compatible sections of $E$ on the $D_f$: the adjunction.
What is left to show
Essential image of $\Phi$ = sheaves; essential image of $\Psi$ = $\operatorname{Et}(X)$.
Stronger statement, via the adjunction maps:
\Psi\Phi(E)\to E\ \ \text{iso}\iff E\ \text{étale over } X
P\to\Phi\Psi(P)\ \ \text{iso}\iff P\ \text{is a sheaf}
Then $\Phi$, $\Psi$ are inverse equivalences $\operatorname{Et}(X)\simeq\operatorname{Top}(X)$.
And $\Phi\Psi\colon\hat{\mathcal O}\to\operatorname{Top}(X)$ is left adjoint to the inclusion: the associated sheaf.
Left exactness of $\Phi\Psi$: reduces to that of $\Psi$, checked on fibres:
\Psi(P)_x=P_x\quad\text{left exact in } P
Étale $E$: fibres of $\Psi\Phi(E)$ at $x$ are germs of sections of $E$.
\Phi(E)_x\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }E_x,\qquad \text{germ}\mapsto\text{value at } x
True for $E$ étale: a germ of section is its value (local open immersion).
$P$ a sheaf: both sides sheaves, compare stalks: $\Phi\Psi(P)_x=\Psi(P)_x=P_x$.
Question from the room: equivalently check full faithfulness. Probably the same work.
Advantage of $\Psi$: gives the equivalence, the adjoint and left exactness together.
A good exercise to work out in detail.
Consequences of the fibre functors
Each $\mathrm{St}_x$: left exact, commutes with all direct limits; family conservative.
u\colon F\to G\ \text{mono}\iff \forall x:\ u_x\colon F_x\to G_x\ \text{injective}
\begin{CD} F @= F\\ @| @VV{u}V\\ F @>{u}>> G \end{CD}
Mono = this square cartesian; $\mathrm{St}_x$ preserves fibre products and detects isomorphisms.
u\colon F\to G\ \text{epi}\iff \forall x:\ u_x\ \text{surjective}
\begin{CD} F @>{u}>> G\\ @V{u}VV @VV{\mathrm{id}}V\\ G @>{\mathrm{id}}>> G \end{CD}
Epi = this square cocartesian ($G=G\sqcup_F G$); check on stalks.
General principle: any statement built with direct limits and finite inverse limits (arrows equal, mono, epi, iso) is checked stalkwise.
